days.title: Harry Potter
days.tagline: Wizarding London: Platform 9¾, the Leaky Cauldron, the Millennium Bridge and the Ministry

films.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1

aboutFilm.short: An orphaned boy learns on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard, and leaves his unkind aunt and uncle for Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Over eight films he and his friends Ron and Hermione face the dark wizard Voldemort.
aboutFilm.more: Based on J.K. Rowling's books, the films ran from 2001 to 2011 with Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint growing up on screen. Most scenes were shot at Leavesden studios, but London plays itself: King's Cross, the City's Victorian markets, the Thames bridges and Whitehall all appear.

days.area: King's Cross, the City, Southwark, Westminster and the West End
days.bestTime: A weekday, or a Saturday with an early start. The Platform 9¾ queue is shortest first thing and long by late morning, especially at weekends and in school holidays. On Sundays the City around Leadenhall is very quiet, which is good for photos but means fewer cafés.
days.intro: Platform 9¾ and the station front are at King's Cross and St Pancras. Leadenhall Market and a blue door off it were Diagon Alley and the Leaky Cauldron, the Death Eaters destroy the Millennium Bridge, and Stoney Street by Borough Market is where the Knight Bus drops Harry. In the afternoon, cross Westminster for Lambeth Bridge and the Ministry of Magic's back streets, and end in the West End by the Harry Potter statue and the stage play.

food.note: Easy all day: King's Cross, Borough Market and Soho are three of London's best areas to eat. The longest stretch without a sit-down café is Westminster in the afternoon, so take a snack from Borough Market.

parking.note: Don't drive. Almost the whole route is inside the central Congestion Charge zone, parking is expensive, and every stop is near a tube station. If you come by car, park outside the centre near a tube station and ride in.
warnings: The central Congestion Charge applies on weekdays and weekends.
London's ULEZ charge applies to older cars across all of London. Check your car on the TfL website before you drive.

gettingThere.note: The day uses two short tube rides: King's Cross to Bank on the Northern line, and London Bridge to Westminster on the Jubilee line. Finish at Leicester Square or Tottenham Court Road.

stops.name: Breakfast at Dishoom King's Cross
stops.about: The bacon naan roll is a London classic. Breakfast here before the 9¾ queue builds.

stops.name: Platform 9¾
stops.scene: The trolley half-through the wall and the official shop. The real scenes were filmed between platforms 4 and 5.
tips: Staff hand you a house scarf for the trolley photo. It's free, but the queue grows fast.

stops.scene: Philosopher's Stone: the station front. Chamber of Secrets: the Weasleys park the flying Ford Anglia here.
tips: The red-brick clock tower is best from across Euston Road.

stops.name: 12 Grimmauld Place

tips: 15 minutes' walk each way. Skip it if the 9¾ queue ran long.

legs.note: Back to King's Cross, then the Northern line to Bank (about 10 minutes), and 5 minutes' walk.
Jubilee line from London Bridge to Westminster (2 stops), then 10 minutes along Millbank.

tips: Most of the films were shot at the studios in Leavesden, so London's real locations are mostly street scenes. The Studio Tour is where the sets are.

extras.title: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
extras.text: The stage play at the Palace Theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue, now a single show of 2 hours 55 minutes. Tickets from £28, age 8 and up, booking until June 2027.

extras.title: Make it two days: Warner Bros. Studio Tour
extras.text: The real sets, from the Great Hall to Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express, at Leavesden outside London. Train from Euston to Watford Junction (about 20 minutes), then the studio shuttle bus. Allow at least 4 hours. Tickets are timed and sell out weeks ahead, so book first.

extras.title: Also in the films
extras.text: The Reptile House at London Zoo, where Harry talks to the python, and Australia House on the Strand (Gringotts' interior, outside only for visitors) are off this route.

days.title: Notting Hill
days.tagline: A day in William and Anna's neighbourhood

aboutFilm.short: William runs a small travel bookshop in Notting Hill. Then Anna Scott, the most famous film star in the world, walks in, and his quiet life is turned upside down.
aboutFilm.more: Richard Curtis wrote it five years after Four Weddings and a Funeral, and Roger Michell directed. Hugh Grant plays William, Julia Roberts plays Anna, and Rhys Ifans nearly steals the film as Spike, William's flatmate. It was one of the biggest British films of 1999, and it turned Portobello Road into a place fans still come to see.

days.bestTime: A Saturday, when Portobello Market is in full swing
days.intro: Almost every location in Notting Hill is on a few streets around Portobello Road, so the whole film fits into one walk. You'll see where William's bookshop was, the corner where he spills orange juice on Anna, the blue door of his flat, the market he walks through as the seasons change, and the garden square they climb into at night. In the evening, finish with dinner and a film at the Electric Cinema.

food.note: You're never more than a few minutes from a café. On Saturdays the market stalls make lunch easy; on weekdays the market is smaller, so use the cafés on Portobello Road and Westbourne Grove.

parking.note: Street parking is pay-by-app and hard to find, especially on market Saturdays. It's easier to leave the car further out and take the tube in.
warnings: London's ULEZ charge applies to older cars across all of London. Check your car on the TfL website before you drive.
Notting Hill is outside the central Congestion Charge zone.

gettingThere.note: Notting Hill Gate is the easiest station to find, and Ladbroke Grove is closest to the later stops if you want to get home from there.

stops.name: Breakfast on Westbourne Grove
stops.about: A brunch strip with plenty of choice, five minutes from Portobello Road.

alternatives.name: Granger & Co
alternatives.why: Australian-style brunch, the classic choice. Queues at weekends

alternatives.name: Farm Girl
alternatives.why: Lighter, healthy plates and good coffee, on the way to the first stop

stops.name: William's shop
stops.scene: The exterior of William's travel bookshop.
tips: It was never a real bookshop. It was an antiques arcade and is now a gift shop with a sign added.

stops.name: The Notting Hill Bookshop
stops.about: The real Travel Bookshop that inspired the film, with film merchandise. The day's dedicated attraction.

stops.name: Books for Cooks
stops.about: Not in the film, but a cookbook shop with a test-kitchen lunch. Worth a browse, or come back for lunch.

stops.name: The orange juice corner
stops.address: Corner of Portobello Road and Westbourne Park Road, W11
stops.scene: William collides with Anna and spills orange juice down her top.
tips: Coffeebello is right on the corner, so this is the coffee stop.

stops.name: Coffeebello
stops.address: Portobello Road, on the corner of Westbourne Park Road, W11
stops.about: Coffee on the spot of the collision.

stops.name: The blue door
stops.scene: William's front door, where Anna turns up and the press camp outside.
tips: This is a private home. Take your photo quickly and quietly, and don't sit on the steps.

stops.name: "I love Ken" tattoo shop
stops.scene: The tattoo parlour in the opening credits.

stops.name: Portobello Market
stops.scene: The "Ain't No Sunshine" walk, where William strolls through a year of seasons, was filmed along the market.
tips: The full market runs on Saturdays. On other days it's much quieter.

stops.name: Lunch at the market
stops.about: Street food from the market stalls: pick and mix, and eat as you browse.

alternatives.name: Books for Cooks
alternatives.why: Sit-down lunch from the test kitchen, small and popular

alternatives.name: Ottolenghi
alternatives.why: Salads and pastries to take away, good for a picnic

alternatives.name: Electric Diner
alternatives.why: American diner food, no fuss, good with children

stops.name: Rosmead Gardens
stops.scene: William and Anna climb in to the locked garden square after the dinner party.
tips: It's a private garden: peek through the railings. It opens to the public only on Open Garden Squares Weekend.

stops.name: The birthday dinner house
stops.scene: The house where William brings Anna to his sister's birthday dinner.

stops.name: The Coronet
stops.scene: The cinema where William watches Anna in Helix.
tips: It's now the Coronet Theatre, so check what's on if you want to go in.

stops.name: Dinner and a film at the Electric Cinema
stops.about: One of London's oldest cinemas, with sofas and footstools. The perfect end to the day.
tips: Book ahead for the front sofas, especially at weekends.

alternatives.name: Electric Diner
alternatives.why: Dinner next door to the cinema before the film

tips: Saturday is market day: busier, but the day comes alive.
Several stops are private homes. Be brief and quiet outside them.

extras.title: Kenwood House, Hampstead Heath
extras.text: Where Anna shoots her period film. Free entry, with a café. Best as a separate morning or afternoon.

extras.title: Afternoon tea at the Ritz
extras.text: Anna's hotel. Lovely, but expensive, and well away from Notting Hill.

days.title: Paddington
days.tagline: A bear's London: Portobello Road, the station, the canal and the Browns' house

aboutFilm.short: A polite young bear from Peru arrives alone at Paddington station with a label round his neck and is taken in by the Brown family. His marmalade, his manners and his talent for chaos slowly win over London.
aboutFilm.more: Ben Whishaw voices Paddington in all three films, with Hugh Bonneville and Sally Hawkins (then Emily Mortimer) as Mr and Mrs Brown. In Paddington 2, Hugh Grant plays the vain actor Phoenix Buchanan, who frames Paddington for theft. Paddington in Peru takes the family back to the jungle to find Aunt Lucy.

days.area: Notting Hill, Little Venice and Primrose Hill
days.bestTime: A Saturday from spring to early autumn, when Portobello Market is at its fullest and the canal waterbus runs a full timetable. Reach Primrose Hill an hour before sunset for the best light.
days.intro: Mr Gruber's antique shop is a real shop on Portobello Road, the bear statue waits under the clock at Paddington station, and the Paddington 2 canal chase runs from Little Venice to Camden Lock. The day ends at the Browns' pastel house on Chalcot Crescent and the view from Primrose Hill, with a canal boat ride in the middle.

food.note: Eating is easy all day: Portobello Road and Camden Market are full of options, and Little Venice has pubs and a café boat. The canal boat itself has nothing, so bring a drink and a snack. A marmalade sandwich is the obvious choice.

parking.note: Not recommended: street parking around Portobello Road is pay-by-app and very hard on market Saturdays, and the walk ends a long way from where it starts. If you drive, park once near Primrose Hill on a side street and take the tube to the start.
warnings: London's ULEZ charge applies to older cars across all of London. Check your car on the TfL website before you drive.
The route is outside the central Congestion Charge zone.

gettingThere.note: The day uses one short tube hop (Notting Hill Gate to Paddington, 2 stops) and finishes at Chalk Farm on the Northern line, 10 minutes from Chalcot Crescent.

stops.name: Breakfast at Farm Girl
stops.about: A bright café at the top of Portobello Road, good for a relaxed breakfast before the market gets busy.

alternatives.name: Granger & Co
alternatives.why: Australian-style breakfast, a bit of a treat

alternatives.name: Market stalls
alternatives.why: Pastries on the go, quick and cheap

stops.name: Mr Gruber's antique shop
stops.scene: Mr Gruber's shop in both films, where Paddington finds the pop-up book of London.
tips: The bright red shopfront photographs best from across the road.

stops.name: Giuseppe's barber shop
stops.address: Portobello Road at Denbigh Terrace, W11
stops.scene: Paddington 2: the salon where Paddington's first job goes badly wrong.
tips: The shopfront was changed digitally for the film, so it won't look quite the same.

stops.name: Portobello Market
stops.scene: Paddington: the skateboard ride through the market.
tips: Best on a Saturday morning, when every stall is out. Grab a coffee from a stall as you walk.

stops.name: Paddington Station statue
stops.address: Platform 1, under the clock, Praed Street, W2
stops.scene: Paddington: where the Browns find a small bear with a label round his neck.
stops.about: The platforms are real, but the tea room was a set.
tips: A second bronze Paddington sits in Merchant Square, by the station's canal exit.

stops.name: Browning's Island, Little Venice
stops.scene: Paddington 2: the canal chase after the robbery.
tips: Walk the canal from Paddington Basin to get here (about 15 minutes).
The best view of the island is from the bridge on Warwick Avenue.

stops.name: The Prince Alfred, and lunch
stops.scene: Paddington: the pub Paddington flies over.
stops.about: A Victorian pub with its original glass screens. Pub food for lunch.

alternatives.name: Waterside Café
alternatives.why: A café on a boat, light and quick

alternatives.name: Raoul's
alternatives.why: Easy café food, good for families

stops.name: "Westbourne Oak" station
stops.address: Maida Vale station, Elgin Avenue, W9
stops.scene: Paddington: the Browns' local tube station.
tips: The red tiled entrance and the station sign are the shot.

stops.name: Camden Lock
stops.scene: Paddington 2: the end of the canal chase.
tips: Photograph the lock gates from the footbridge.

stops.name: Camden Market street food
stops.about: Dozens of street food stalls, so everyone picks their own. Good for teens.

alternatives.name: Ice cream at the lock
alternatives.why: A quick treat if you had a big lunch

stops.name: Phoenix Buchanan's house
stops.scene: Paddington 2: the vain actor's home.
tips: A private home, so photograph from the square.

stops.name: The Browns' house, "Windsor Gardens"
stops.scene: All three films: the Browns' home on the curve of pastel houses.
tips: A private home, so be brief and quiet.
Tea and cake on Regent's Park Road, Primrose Hill's café street, is two minutes away.

stops.name: Primrose Hill summit
stops.about: Not a film stop, but the best free view of London and the right place for a final photo. Dinner on Regent's Park Road or back in Camden, then home from Chalk Farm.

legs.note: Walk back to Notting Hill Gate, then the Circle or District line to Paddington (2 stops).
Walk back to Little Venice for the waterbus to Camden Lock (book ahead; reduced in winter). Or walk the Regent's Canal towpath, about 75 minutes.

tips: The waterbus runs less often in winter, and sometimes only at weekends. Check the timetable before you go, or walk the towpath instead.

extras.title: The Paddington Bear Experience
extras.text: An immersive 70-minute family show at County Hall on the South Bank, tickets from £44. It is listed to close on 31 December 2026. It can replace the canal boat: after lunch, take the Bakerloo line from Warwick Avenue to Waterloo.

extras.title: Paddington in Leicester Square
extras.text: A Paddington statue is part of the Scenes in the Square trail in Leicester Square, listed until November 2027.

extras.title: Also in the films
extras.text: The Natural History Museum (Millicent's workplace), the Shard (Mr Brown's office) and Tower Bridge and St Paul's from the Paddington 2 clue hunt are all off this route.

days.title: Ted Lasso
days.tagline: Believe in Richmond: Ted's pub, his street and the river

films.title: Ted Lasso
films.director: Created by Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt and Joe Kelly

aboutFilm.short: An American college football coach is hired to manage AFC Richmond, a struggling English football club, even though he knows nothing about the game. His relentless kindness slowly wins over the players, the owner and the town.
aboutFilm.more: Jason Sudeikis plays Ted, with Hannah Waddingham as the club's owner Rebecca and Brett Goldstein as the gruff captain Roy Kent. The Apple TV+ series ran for three seasons from 2020 to 2023 and won the Emmy for best comedy series twice.

days.bestTime: Any day of the week. Mornings are quieter on Richmond Green, and a dry day makes the riverside walk to Twickenham a highlight.
days.intro: The show's Richmond is real: Ted's local pub, the lane where he lives and the Green where he meets the town are all a few minutes from Richmond station. In the afternoon, follow the Thames to Twickenham for Church Street and the riverside bench from Season 2, then head back to Richmond for dinner by the river.

food.note: Richmond and Twickenham have plenty of pubs and cafés, but the riverside path between them has almost nothing for about 45 minutes. Bring water, and a snack if you're walking it with children.

parking.note: Richmond town centre parking is pay-and-display and fills up at weekends. The nearest larger car park is listed below.
warnings: London's ULEZ charge applies to older cars across all of London. Check your car on the TfL website before you drive.
Richmond is outside the central Congestion Charge zone.

gettingThere.note: Richmond station is the start and the end of the day. From Twickenham you can take a train back, one or two stops.

stops.name: Richmond Green
stops.scene: Ted crosses the Green on his way to work, and a young girl dribbles a ball past him.

stops.name: The Prince's Head (the Crown and Anchor)
stops.scene: The Crown and Anchor, Ted's local, where Mae pours the pints and the fans gather on match days.
tips: The pub's outside is the one in the show, but the bar inside was rebuilt in a studio.

stops.name: Paved Court: Ted's street
stops.scene: The narrow lane where Ted lives, which he walks down on his way to the Green.

stops.name: Coffee in the lanes
stops.address: The lanes between Richmond Green and George Street
stops.about: The lanes around Paved Court are full of independent cafés. Pick one and take your coffee down to the river.

stops.name: Richmond riverside and bridge
stops.about: Not a scene from the show, but the classic view of Richmond: the 18th-century bridge and the terraces down to the Thames.

stops.name: Lunch at the Prince's Head
stops.about: A proper pub lunch in Ted's local. Sit outside facing the Green if the weather allows.

alternatives.name: Chango
alternatives.why: Argentine empanadas to take away. The shop itself appears on Ted's street

stops.name: Church Street, Twickenham
stops.scene: Season 2 scenes on this old village street, including the shopfront used for "Mojo", the doll shop.
tips: Church Street is closed to traffic at weekends, with café tables out in the road.

stops.name: Twickenham riverside, opposite Eel Pie Island
stops.scene: The boathouse and the riverside bench where Roy, Keeley and Phoebe sit and talk.
tips: The Barmy Arms pub is right here if you want a drink by the water before heading back.

stops.name: Dinner at Gaucho Richmond
stops.scene: Thought to be the restaurant from the double-date scene. Not yet confirmed.
stops.about: Argentine steak on the river, a treat to end the day.

alternatives.name: The Prince's Head
alternatives.why: Back to Ted's local for a cheaper, more relaxed dinner

legs.note: Along the Thames towpath past Marble Hill House. Or take a bus or the train (Richmond to Twickenham) if it's raining.
Train from Twickenham back to Richmond, then a short walk down to the river.

tips: Ted Lasso is filmed all over south-west London. This day keeps to the places you can walk between.
The Prince's Head gets busy when the show has a new season out. Go early for an outside table.

extras.title: A match at Selhurst Park
extras.text: Crystal Palace's ground in South Norwood stood in for AFC Richmond's "Nelson Road" stadium. Going to a Palace home game is as close as you'll get to a Richmond match day.

extras.title: Hampton Court Palace
extras.text: A short trip from Twickenham, with its own film and TV location tour. Good for a second day in the area.
